Team —

Attaching the initial artifacts for the upcoming sterile-site deployment test on 2027-02-10. This thread is to lock the forensics & operator checklist we will hand to EdgeGrid couriers and on-site operators. Key asks:

- Confirm the manifest signature format and verification steps (we've signd the manifest with our signing key and attached bundle_manifest.json.sig).
- Approve the pre-install integrity audit steps (hashes, signature verification, operator attestation).
- Decide operator access window and revocation cadence post-install (how long keys remain active for operator troubleshooting).
- Add any telemetry/collection points we must include for compliance (logs retained, hash archives).

Attachments: bundle_manifest.json.sig, operator_checklist_v1.pdf

Notes: I want the forensics checklist to be minimal for operators (one page) but link to a secondary playbook for deeper investigation. If EdgeGrid needs different courier metadata, call it out.

Next step: Priyom, can you add the pre-install audit step set? Rishi, please draft a short forensic capture runbook we can hand the operator (no raw logs shipped off-site).

Thanks —

Laura —

Thanks, looks good overall. A few quick proposals inline:

- Add a "pre-install integrity audit" step: operator runs a short script (sha512sum against each image file and the manifest) and records the output to the on-site acceptance log before flashing.
- Include explicit operator attestation wording: operator signs the acceptance log locally (PGP or HSM token) and we capture the signature blob in the post-install package.
- Revocation: recommend automatic operator key revocation 48 hours after activation unless a scheduled troubleshooting window is opened.

Small quibble: the checklist currently assumes SHA-256; given bundle sizes and our preference for defense-in-depth, I'd push SHA-512 for the courier-level audit (we can still publish SHA-256 in the manifest for quick checks). EdgeGrid: can you confirm courier tools can produce sha512?

I can update operator_checklist_v1.pdf to include the minimal script and attestation stanza — will send v1.1 after I get confirmation.

—Priyom

Hi Laura / Priyom —

Thanks for the draft. Quick responses from the EdgeGrid ops side:

- We can produce SHA-512 checksums and include them alongside SHA-256 in our courier manifest. We prefer the manifest to include a per-file size, SHA-256, and SHA-512 entry.
- Our courier manifest format (attached stub) has fields for carrier_id, chain_of_custody_events, and tamper_seal_ids — please confirm if Redwood wants any of those values mirrored in the signed manifest.
- For operator attestation: our standard flow is HSM-backed operator signing (YubiKey or HSM agent). We can capture the operator signature blob and seal it to the courier manifest; however, EdgeGrid policy requires operator signing keys be rotated on a 30-day cadence. We understand Redwood wants a 48-hour auto-revoke; we can support short-lived delegated tokens for the activation window instead of long-lived operator keys.

Attachment: courier_manifest_stub.txt

We also need a short definition of "forensic capture" you want performed on-site (e.g., preserve /var/log/redwood/install.log, copy of manifest, hash outputs). If you want us to ship a sealed USB with the capture bundle back to Redwood, we can do that under a courier seal process.

—EdgeGrid Operations

Subject: Re: Offline bundle forensics & operator checklist

Laura / Team —

I've drafted a concise forensics capture & post-install verification runbook to hand to operators. High level (this will be published in full in the forensics_playbook_v2.md attachment):

1) Pre-install (arrival):
   - Verify courier_manifest fields: carrier_id, tamper_seal_id, file sizes.
   - Verify manifest signature (verify bundle_manifest.json.sig against Redwood's release key).
   - Run sha512sum on each image file, compare to manifest, record output to acceptance_log.txt.
   - Operator performs HSM-backed attestation signing acceptance_log.txt; capture signature blob and append to sealed_manifest.log.

2) Install (execution):
   - Minimal live capture: tail -n 500 /var/log/redwood/install.log to capture any runtime errors.
   - Record the output of dd if=/dev/sdX | sha256sum for the flashed device (hashing device contents).
   - If a hardware failure occurs, mark package as 'quarantined' and perform local snapshot (write-protected) for post-mortem.

3) Post-install (30min window):
   - Operator submits sealed_manifest.log and acceptance_log.txt to courier for return (sealed USB or encrypted upload to temporary S3 via EdgeGrid-token).
   - Redwood will validate signature blobs and run a second-pass integrity check within 24h.

4) Retention & privacy:
   - No raw customer data leaves the site. Installation logs are redacted to exclude request payloads. Forensic artifacts retained for 90 days unless extended by legal or incident response.

5) Escalation:
   - If post-install verification fails, operator toggles switch to rollback image (GUID provided in manifest) and contacts Redwood on-call. We keep a 4-hour remediation SLA for sealed-site rollbacks.

EdgeGrid — your suggested short-lived delegated tokens for the activation window sound good. We should codify the token issuance/expiration process in the playbook.

Attachment: forensics_playbook_v2.md (draft)

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
